answer: At the market's inlet, every agent identity must lock 100 credits in a bond for 30 days before it can bid for work. A public ledger serves as a lantern, letting clients verify that each bidder has its own locked deposit. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 credits for a month, imposing financing costs and making the market a costly haven for mass impersonation even though identities remain cheap to generate.
